source: សៀវភៅ 'មធ្យោបាយប្រើប្រាស់ឧបករណ៍ព្រោះជាជួរ' (How to Use the Row/Drum Seeder Tool), presented by an agricultural extension teacher for the Agricultural Productivity Enhancement Project in the West Tonle Sap area (APPP) / CAVAC (Cambodia Agricultural Value Chain program), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries -- Battambang provincial department, 2014
text: Recommended water management after drum-seeding rice: keep the field drained or nearly dry for the first 1-3 days after seeding so the seed does not float or wash into clumps, then bring in irrigation water gradually rather than flooding suddenly; after about 24 hours of this gradual flooding the seed's roots should already be anchored in the soil. Rice seedlings typically emerge visibly above the mud within about 4-5 days of sowing. The source also covers building a small levee/bund to hold irrigation water in the plot, having a reserve water source ready to top up the field, and providing drainage so excess water can be released if the field has too much standing water -- all timed around the seed and young seedling's tolerance rather than a fixed calendar.
